projects.title: Jakarta Retail Site Selection
projects.description: Location intelligence platform scoring every H3 hexagon in DKI Jakarta for retail and F&B opportunity, built from 289,000 Overture Maps POIs with BigQuery and dbt. Interactive map included.
projects.longDescription: A site-selection platform for retail and F&B expansion across DKI Jakarta. It ingests 289,015 OpenStreetMap-derived points of interest from Overture Maps, assigns each to an H3 resolution 8 hexagon, and classifies them as F&B competitors or demand generators (offices, education, retail anchors, lodging, lifestyle, health, leisure). dbt on BigQuery then scores every hexagon on demand density, category diversity, and competition, with the weights exposed as dbt variables and enforced by data tests. The result is an interactive MapLibre map with 1,564 scored cells, KPI summary, drill-down detail per cell, and a documented methodology with honest caveats.

stats.data modeling: dbt (20 passing data tests, weights as variables)
stats.cost: Always-free GCP tier plus one small Dataflow batch job

highlights: Ingested and flattened 289,015 Overture Maps places for the DKI Jakarta bounding box, from GeoParquet through Cloud Storage into BigQuery.
Assigned every place to an H3 resolution 8 hexagon with the reference h3 library, the same grid Overture uses, then kept all business logic in dbt on BigQuery.
Classified 1,062 distinct POI categories into competitor and demand-generator roles using lists derived from the actual data distribution, not assumptions.
Scored 1,564 hexagons on demand density, category diversity, and competition, with the weights exposed as dbt variables and data tests enforcing a 0 to 100 range.
Built an interactive MapLibre dashboard with metric switching, score filtering, tier selection, per-cell drill-down, and lazy-loaded category detail.

projects.title: Demand-Driven Replenishment Optimization
projects.description: An ML demand forecast feeding safety-stock and reorder-point decisions, scored in an inventory simulation. Fill rate rose from 81% to 98% and total cost fell 88% against a naive days-of-supply policy.
projects.longDescription: A replenishment decision system for multi-store retail. A gradient-boosted demand forecast sizes each store's safety stock from its own forecast error, which sets the reorder point and base-stock level. Every policy is scored in a period-by-period inventory simulation with supplier lead time, review period, and backorders, tracking fill rate, stockout units, average on-hand, and cost. Each store's service level is then chosen to minimize simulated total cost, and a limited inventory budget is allocated across stores by marginal fill-rate gain per unit of holding cost. In a synthetic backtest against a naive days-of-supply policy, fill rate rose from 81% to 98% and total cost fell 88%. Orchestrated with Dagster.

stats.total cost: down 88% against a naive days-of-supply policy
stats.policy: safety stock z * sigma * sqrt(protection period), reorder point, base stock
stats.simulation: period-by-period model with lead time, review period, and backorders
stats.optimization: per-store service level (0.50 to 0.99) minimizing total cost

highlights: Turned a demand forecast into decisions: safety stock sized from forecast error, then a reorder point and base stock.
Built an inventory simulation with lead time, review period, and backorders, so the policy cost is measured rather than assumed.
Chose each store's service level by minimizing simulated total cost, making the holding-versus-stockout trade-off explicit.
Allocated a limited inventory budget across stores by marginal fill-rate gain per unit of holding cost.
Backtested against a naive days-of-supply baseline: fill rate 81% to 98%, total cost down 88%.

projects.title: Promotion Lift and Trade Optimization
projects.description: Estimating incremental promotion lift with a counterfactual baseline, controlled price elasticity, and incremental margin, then planning a promotion calendar under a fixed trade budget with mixed-integer programming.
projects.longDescription: A causal promotion analytics system. A no-promo demand baseline trained on non-promoted store-weeks provides the counterfactual, so incremental units and margin can be separated from volume that would have sold anyway. Price elasticity is estimated two ways: naively on price alone, and controlled for discount depth, display, season, and store fixed effects, which exposes the confounding when price only moves during promotions. A lift curve maps discount depth to observed-versus-counterfactual demand, and incremental margin charges the discount on every promoted unit. Finally, a mixed-integer program selects at most one discount depth per store-week to maximize incremental margin under a fixed trade budget and a per-store frequency cap. In a synthetic panel, 55 percent of promotions were margin-negative and reallocating the same budget moved margin from -143.6M to +321.4M.

stats.counterfactual: no-promo baseline trained on non-promoted store-weeks
stats.optimization: MILP under a fixed budget plus a per-store frequency cap

highlights: Built the counterfactual no-promo baseline that makes incremental promotion margin computable at all.
Showed the confounding directly: naive price elasticity -0.25 versus controlled -1.45 against a true -1.5.
Charged the discount on every promoted unit, not just the incremental ones, so margin is not overstated.
Planned a promotion calendar with a mixed-integer program under a fixed budget and a per-store frequency cap.
Found that 55% of promotions destroyed margin, and turned the same budget from -143.6M to +321.4M.

projects.title: Retail Demand Forecasting with AI
projects.description: Store-level demand forecasting for multi-branch retail: gradient-boosted daily sales prediction with walk-forward validation, an honest naive-baseline comparison, and a GenAI layer that turns forecasts into store recommendations.
projects.longDescription: A store-level demand forecasting system for multi-branch retail. A gradient-boosted model predicts each store's daily sales up to 30 days ahead, using calendar, promotion, lag, and rolling features from the sales history. The model is validated walk-forward on the last 30 days per store and scored with MAE, RMSE, and MAPE against a naive lag-7 baseline, so the accuracy claim has a reference point. Because future lags are unknown, the horizon forecast feeds on the model's own predictions. A GenAI layer turns the numeric forecast into plain-language, store-specific recommendations for operations teams, with a fully offline heuristic fallback when no API key is present. Orchestrated with Dagster.

stats.baseline: 44.8% lower MAE than a naive lag-7 forecast
stats.validation: walk-forward holdout, last 30 days per store
stats.model: HistGradientBoostingRegressor over calendar, lag, and rolling features
stats.insight layer: LLM with an offline heuristic fallback

highlights: Engineered calendar, promotion, lag, and rolling-window features that capture weekly seasonality and recent store momentum.
Validated walk-forward instead of a random split, so no future information leaks into training.
Compared against a naive lag-7 baseline and reported a 44.8% reduction in MAE rather than an unanchored score.
Produced a 30-day per-store forecast iteratively, using the model's own predictions because future lags do not exist.
Added a GenAI insight layer that converts forecasts into store-specific recommendations, with an offline fallback when no API key is set.

projects.title: Streaming CDC Pipeline with Debezium and Kafka
projects.description: Change data capture end to end: Postgres logical decoding via Debezium into Kafka, then a Python consumer writing an idempotent ClickHouse sink. At-least-once delivery made effectively-once, with dead-letter routing, consumer-lag metrics, and Dagster orchestration.
projects.longDescription: A production-shaped CDC pipeline built to exercise the parts of streaming that actually break: offset handling, duplicate delivery, deletes, poison messages, and schema-shaped payloads. Postgres runs with wal_level=logical; a Debezium connector decodes the write-ahead log into JSON envelopes on Kafka topics. A Python consumer decodes the envelope, transforms it into the sink row shape, batches by size or interval, writes to ClickHouse, and only then commits offsets, so a crash replays at most one batch. Replays are harmless because every row carries the source change timestamp as _version and ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree(_version, is_deleted) keeps the highest version per key. Deletes become soft flags, so an older replay cannot resurrect a row. Poison messages are routed to a dead-letter topic with x-error and x-origin-topic headers instead of stalling the pipeline. Comes with 27 offline tests (no broker required), CI, and an eight-lab study guide that breaks the pipeline on purpose.
highlights: Write-then-commit ordering asserted by a test, so a crash replays instead of losing data.
Source-timestamp versioning plus ReplacingMergeTree makes replays and deletes converge to one truth.
Poison messages go to a dead-letter topic with error context instead of stalling the consumer.
Documented honestly as effectively-once, not exactly-once.

projects.title: Earthquake Analytics Pipeline
projects.description: End-to-end Google Cloud data platform over approximately 500,000 earthquake events. Terraform-provisioned infrastructure, Kestra orchestration, and a BigQuery warehouse partitioned by month and clustered for query cost-efficiency.
projects.longDescription: An end-to-end data platform built to ingest, process, and analyze approximately 500,000 earthquake events from the USGS catalog (2015 to 2025). Infrastructure is fully provisioned with Terraform, ingestion runs as a monthly Kestra batch into Cloud Storage, and dbt models the data in three layers: staging, intermediate, and marts. The BigQuery fact table is partitioned by month and clustered by magnitude category and region, which keeps dashboard queries fast and cheap. The result is an interactive Looker Studio report that is embedded directly in the case study.

stats.FinOps optimization: Minimized compute costs via partitioned fact tables

highlights: Developed a fully automated, version-controlled cloud infrastructure using Terraform for GCP setup.
Designed a resilient, monthly ingestion pipeline utilizing Kestra workflows with built-in retries.
Engineered a layered BigQuery warehouse, partitioning tables by month and clustering by magnitude category and region to optimize scan volumes and reduce querying costs.
Modeled robust SQL transformations with dbt across staging, intermediate, and marts layers.
Created an interactive Looker Studio report, embedded on this site, with sub-second report response times.

projects.title: FreshCart E-commerce Analytics Pipeline
projects.description: Production-grade e-commerce analytics platform orchestrating a 7-task Airflow pipeline. Features a medallion data warehouse structure, customer RFM behavior segmentation, and automated testing preventing schema drift.
projects.longDescription: A robust batch ETL data platform orchestrating the flow of 150K+ transactional records. Powered by Apache Airflow (Docker LocalExecutor), the pipeline automatically ingests data to Google Cloud Storage and loads it to BigQuery. Using dbt, the data is transformed across Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers. Built-in SQL algorithms compute RFM segmentation to group customers into 10 behavioral profiles for marketing activation, while 20+ data quality assertions protect downstream BI stability.
highlights: Orchestrated a 7-task parallel Apache Airflow DAG on a Dockerized LocalExecutor, automating raw extraction, GCS loading, and multi-tier dbt compilation.
Designed a SQL-native RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) analytics model directly in dbt, grouping buyers into actionable marketing segments like Champions, Loyalists, and At-Risk.
Implemented 20+ automated data quality constraints (primary key uniqueness, category domain checks) to enforce data integrity.
Engineered a medallion architecture in BigQuery to isolate raw streams (Bronze) from analytics-ready business models (Gold).
Constructed high-density Looker Studio dashboards visualizing customer cohort retention, revenue trends, and catalog product rankings.

projects.title: AI-Native RAG Ingestion Pipeline
projects.description: Modular background ingestion pipeline parsing unstructured files, generating local dense vector embeddings, and serving semantic search queries via FastAPI.
projects.longDescription: A production-grade, secure, and self-contained Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) backend data platform. It parses raw unstructured documents, splits them into semantic text chunks using recursive splitters, generates dense vector representations locally using sentence-transformers, and stores them in Qdrant. Exposes FastAPI endpoints for semantic search and prompt-engineered RAG queries.

stats.security layers: SSRF scheme filter + request length restrictions

highlights: Implemented local open-source dense vector embeddings using SentenceTransformers, completely eliminating third-party API dependencies.
Created a resilient database client wrapper that automatically falls back to local disk-based storage if the server connection fails.
Built strict query length validation and secure protocol scheme Allow-lists to mitigate SSRF and buffer-overflow security risks.
Designed custom prompt engineering context builders to feed local Ollama LLMs with relevant source metadata.
Developed a containerized stack utilizing Docker Compose and automated testing suites via FastAPI TestClient.

projects.title: E-commerce Data Analysis
projects.description: End-to-end analysis of a public e-commerce dataset: SQL exploration and cleaning, RFM customer segmentation, and a Power BI dashboard of sales trends.
projects.longDescription: A complete data analysis workflow answering three business questions: who are the most valuable customers, which products drive revenue, and how do sales trend over time. The dataset is explored and cleaned in SQL (nulls, duplicates, date ranges), customers are segmented with RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) analysis, and the results are delivered as a Power BI dashboard for business stakeholders.
highlights: Explored the dataset in SQL: schema inventory, null checks, duplicate detection, and date-range profiling.
Cleaned and standardized data: status/category normalization, invalid-amount handling, and derived time dimensions.
Built an RFM segmentation model grouping customers into Champions, Loyal, At-Risk, and Lost segments.
Delivered findings as a Power BI dashboard covering sales trends, category performance, and segment value.

projects.title: Modern Data Warehouse with DuckDB
projects.description: Bronze → Silver → Gold data pipeline built with DuckDB and Python, demonstrating the Medallion Architecture end-to-end.
projects.longDescription: A hands-on implementation of a modern data warehouse stack. Raw CSV files are ingested into a Bronze layer as-is, cleansed and deduplicated into Silver, then modeled into star-schema marts in Gold — all with DuckDB and Python, no server required. Includes runnable sample data and a monthly revenue query against the final mart.
highlights: Implemented a three-layer medallion pipeline: raw Bronze ingestion, cleansed Silver layer, and analytics-ready Gold marts.
Used DuckDB for an embedded, zero-infrastructure data warehouse experience.
Modeled gold.fact_sales and gold.dim_customer following star-schema conventions.
Ships with sample data and a monthly revenue query, runnable with a single command.
